+// the palette lists four banner dyes (white, black, brown, orange) and wall hanging signs, not every dye or wall sign the

+const BANNER_DYE = { light_gray: "white", red: "brown" };
+const withNbt = (nbt, key, value) => nbt && { ...nbt, value: { ...nbt.value, [key]: value } };
+// the block a vocabulary write lands as, and its block entity (sign text, banner patterns) to match
+function paletteBlock(block, state, nbt) {
+  const sign = /^((?:minecraft:)?)(\w+)_wall_sign$/.exec(block);
+  if (sign) return { block: `${sign[1]}${sign[2]}_wall_hanging_sign`, state, nbt: withNbt(nbt, "id", { type: "string", value: "minecraft:hanging_sign" }) };
+  const banner = /^((?:minecraft:)?)(\w+)_wall_banner$/.exec(block);

content.text: The NBT check found a flaw in my colour rule: a border pattern kept the old dye (`border:light_gray` on a white cloth, `border:red` on a brown one). The border should take the new cloth colour, and only letters that now clash should get the contrast colour. Fixing that:

lines: if (sign) return { block: `${sign[1]}${sign[2]}_wall_hanging_sign`, state, nbt: withNbt(nbt, "id", { type: "string", value: "minecraft:hanging_sign" }) };
const banner = /^((?:minecraft:)?)(\w+)_wall_banner$/.exec(block);
if (!banner || !BANNER_DYE[banner[2]]) return { block, state, nbt };
-  const dye = BANNER_DYE[banner[2]], pats = nbt?.value?.patterns;
-  // a letter in the cloth's own dye would vanish into it, so those letters take the contrast
-  const fixed = (pats?.value?.value ?? []).map((p) => (p.color.value === dye ? { ...p, color: { type: "string", value: dye === "white" ? "black" : "white" } } : p));
+  const old = banner[2], dye = BANNER_DYE[old], pats = nbt?.value?.patterns;
+  const contrast = dye === "white" ? "black" : "white";
+  // the cloth's own colour (the border) moves to the new cloth; a letter that now shares the cloth's dye would vanish, so it takes the contrast
+  const fixed = (pats?.value?.value ?? []).map((p) => {
+    if (p.color.value === old) return { ...p, color: { type: "string", value: dye } };
+    if (p.color.value === dye) return { ...p, color: { type: "string", value: contrast } };
+    return p;
return { block: `${banner[1]}${dye}_wall_banner`, state, nbt: pats ? withNbt(nbt, "patterns", { ...pats, value: { ...pats.value, value: fixed } }) : nbt };

left: Wall banners are not in palette.json (it lists white_banner, black_banner, brown_banner, orange_banner only), so the fascia letters still report OFF-PALETTE: white_wall_banner x14, brown_wall_banner x12, black_wall_banner x5.
